entries.authority_implication: The umbrella term grants no authority; identify the actual parent control plane.

disambiguation.meaning: any system in which multiple agents interact

entries.example: In the Loop is a MAS whose specific control architecture is manager orchestrated.
entries.plain_english: A system in which more than one agent contributes to an outcome.
entries.technical_definition: The industry umbrella for interacting agent components; it does not specify who controls routing or authority.

entries.authority_implication: Questions, approvals, commands, counters, joins, and protected effects remain here.

disambiguation.meaning: the sole human-facing graph controller

entries.example: The parent asks for commit approval after joining the audit and boundary results.
entries.plain_english: The one session that stays responsible for decisions and coordinates all child work.
entries.technical_definition: The sole control plane that drives the graph, enforces limits, owns interaction and protected effects, and consolidates results.

entries.authority_implication: An atomic agent receives only the access and authority in its task envelope.

disambiguation.meaning: one bounded custom-agent profile

entries.example: The analyst is an atomic read-only agent; it is not a workflow.
entries.plain_english: One specialist profile given one bounded task.
entries.technical_definition: A single role/model/access profile dispatched by the parent under the shared task and result contracts.

entries.authority_implication: The parent still drives every node; composition does not create an unattended controller.

disambiguation.meaning: a reusable parent-driven .itl.md graph

entries.example: repo_factory is a composite agent that routes bounded nodes to atomic capabilities.
entries.plain_english: A reusable recipe that combines several bounded agent steps.
entries.technical_definition: A declarative .itl.md workflow whose component and agent nodes are validated, flattened, locked, and driven by the parent.

entries.authority_implication: Loading instructions does not authorize actions or prove execution.

disambiguation.meaning: instructions loaded for a task

entries.example: The repo-factory skill tells the parent how to drive the repo_factory workflow.
entries.plain_english: Reusable guidance that helps a session perform a kind of work.
entries.technical_definition: An instruction surface consumed by the active session, distinct from a delegated profile or graph declaration.

entries.authority_implication: A workflow file declares control; it does not execute itself or grant authority.

disambiguation.meaning: a declarative graph driven by the parent

entries.example: The parent validates and locks repo-factory.itl.md before dispatch.
entries.plain_english: A checked file describing which bounded steps connect and when they may run.
entries.technical_definition: A versioned declarative orchestration graph with state, routing, limits, and node contracts; it is not executable code.

entries.authority_implication: State may carry declared data and counters, never implicit approval.

disambiguation.meaning: declared data shared through explicit mappings

entries.example: findings and delegations_so_far are workflow state; commit approval is not.
entries.plain_english: The explicit data and counters the workflow is allowed to carry between steps.
entries.technical_definition: Typed graph data whose component inputs and returns cross only declared mappings and accumulator rules.

entries.authority_implication: Context informs work but never grants or restores authority.

disambiguation.meaning: selected information relevant to the bounded task

entries.example: A component map and source digests can be context without authorizing a commit.
entries.plain_english: The relevant information supplied so a task can be understood correctly.
entries.technical_definition: Versioned task or architecture inputs selected for relevance; context is separate from authority and observable evidence.

entries.authority_implication: Persisted memory cannot restore approval, credentials, prompts, or repair authority.

disambiguation.meaning: declared safe state, not hidden conversational memory

entries.example: A checkpoint may retain counters but must reject an approved_to_push field.
entries.plain_english: Only explicitly allowed workflow progress may be saved for later resumption.
entries.technical_definition: Digest-bound projected state and counters under the same lock, recursively excluding private and authority-shaped content.

entries.authority_implication: Only the human-approved revision and digest control implementation; a draft grants no authority.

disambiguation.meaning: a separate decision-complete, digest-bound implementation basis

entries.example: Plan P1 binds scope, interfaces, tests, exclusions, and release limitations.
entries.plain_english: The agreed implementation design, distinct from the original idea and from permission to perform protected effects.
entries.technical_definition: A revisioned and digested record of architecture, behavior, verification, risks, dependencies, exclusions, and authority boundaries.

entries.authority_implication: State the exact effect, target, and candidate; do not infer approval from tone or context.

disambiguation.meaning: human authority for one specifically bounded action

entries.example: Approval to edit the workspace is not approval to commit or push.
entries.plain_english: Explicit human permission for a clearly named action.
entries.technical_definition: A bounded authority grant subject to the active host, sandbox, repository, and human policy; it is not serializable state.

entries.authority_implication: Prove-only audit may inspect and probe but cannot repair without separate authority.

disambiguation.meaning: candidate generation followed by reproducible proof or clearance

entries.example: A symlink concern becomes an audit finding only after a copied-tree probe reproduces the false pass.
entries.plain_english: A proof-first review that tests possible risks and keeps false positives visible.
entries.technical_definition: A bounded lifecycle that orients, scouts candidates, proves or clears them, optionally repairs with authority, verifies regressions, and obtains closure.

entries.authority_implication: A finding names a repair owner but does not itself authorize the repair.

disambiguation.meaning: a candidate whose criterion and impact were reproduced

entries.example: The symlink false pass was a finding because the exact temporary-tree probe exited zero before repair.
entries.plain_english: A suspected problem that a repeatable check has actually demonstrated.
entries.technical_definition: A candidate promoted only after reproducible evidence meets its declared criterion and impact, with an assigned fix owner.

entries.authority_implication: Resume restores safe progress only and requires any needed approval again.

disambiguation.meaning: canonical same-lock progress and safe state

entries.example: A checkpoint can restore delegations_so_far but not repair_authority.
entries.plain_english: A safe record that lets the parent continue verified progress after interruption.
entries.technical_definition: A canonical digest-bound projection of legal completed-node prefix, counters, safe state, and evidence references under one exact lock.

entries.authority_implication: An app connection exposes tools; using a protected external effect still requires active authority.

disambiguation.meaning: an external service connection surfaced as callable tools

entries.example: A connected app can expose service tools, while the In the Loop plugin deliberately exposes none.
entries.plain_english: A connection that lets Codex use tools from another service.
entries.technical_definition: A binding capability that exposes an external service's operations through configured connector tools; it is distinct from the plugin bundle.

entries.authority_implication: Inspect the manifest; installing or publishing a plugin is a separate protected effect.

disambiguation.meaning: a bundle declaring one or more supported capability surfaces

entries.example: In the Loop is a plugin whose current manifest declares exactly a skills directory.
entries.plain_english: A distributable extension bundle; what it provides depends on its manifest.
entries.technical_definition: A platform packaging boundary that may declare supported capabilities, while this repository's Codex plugin intentionally remains skills-only.

entries.authority_implication: Local readiness does not authorize commit, push, publication, marketplace mutation, or deployment.

disambiguation.meaning: tested, documented, audited, packaged, and independently closed on the local candidate

entries.example: A verified Git bundle can be locally release-ready while nothing has been pushed.
entries.plain_english: The local candidate has passed its required checks and review, but has not been released.
entries.technical_definition: An evidence state bound to exact local bytes, qualification, artifact identity, and independent closure, excluding remote effects.

entries.authority_implication: A remote release requires separate explicit approval and direct observation of the effect.

disambiguation.meaning: an authorized release effect was actually performed and observed

entries.example: A marketplace publication is a remote release; creating a local bundle is not.
entries.plain_english: The authorized result has actually been made available through its intended remote channel.
entries.technical_definition: A separately authorized and observed publication, deployment, marketplace, or equivalent remote delivery effect.

entries.authority_implication: Name whether production means local qualification or a live environment; never infer deployment.

disambiguation.meaning: tested, documented, audited, packaged, and locally release-ready
a user-facing deployed environment

entries.example: This curriculum may be production-qualified locally without being deployed to production.
entries.plain_english: Either a rigorously qualified candidate or the actual live environment; the speaker must say which.
entries.technical_definition: An overloaded delivery term that must distinguish evidence-backed local readiness from an authorized and observed live deployment.

entries.authority_implication: Check the global and local cycle maxima before dispatch; changing roles does not reset them.

disambiguation.meaning: one owner-directed return to repair followed by regression verification

entries.example: repo_factory permits at most two owner-directed repair cycles.
entries.plain_english: One controlled return to the responsible repair step, with a hard stopping count.
entries.technical_definition: A guarded backward workflow transition that consumes both a delegation and cycle counter before dispatch.
